nameStory: The wavy lamellaria gets its common name from the undulating, wave-like patterns that ripple across its soft body and shell. The scientific name 'undata' comes from the Latin word for 'wavy,' perfectly capturing this sea snail's most distinctive feature.
description: The wavy lamellaria is a small sea snail that lives in New England's coastal waters. Like other marine gastropods (a fancy name for snails and slugs), it has a soft body that it can pull into its shell for protection. These tiny mollusks are part of the velutinidae family, known for their relatively smooth shells and marine lifestyle. They're quite small, typically measuring less than an inch across.

idTips.label: Wavy body patterns
idTips.description: Look for distinctive undulating, wave-like ridges or patterns across the soft body tissue when the animal is extended from its shell

idTips.label: Small spiral shell
idTips.description: Shell is typically smooth to the touch with a low, flattened spiral shape that feels delicate between your fingers

idTips.label: Marine habitat
idTips.description: Always found in saltwater environments, never in freshwater ponds or streams

idTips.label: Soft body texture
idTips.description: When extended, the body feels slimy and smooth, similar to touching the underside of a garden slug

habitat: Wavy lamellaria are found in New England's marine coastal waters, likely in shallow areas with rocky substrates or among seaweed beds. Given their rarity in observations, they may prefer specific microhabitats such as tide pools or areas with particular water temperatures and salinity levels.

seasonality.spring: May become more active as water temperatures begin to warm, though specific seasonal behaviors are not well documented for this rare species.
seasonality.summer: Likely most active during warmer months when marine life is generally more observable in New England waters.
seasonality.fall: Activity may decrease as water temperatures cool, potentially moving to deeper or more protected areas.
seasonality.winter: Probably least active during cold months, seeking shelter in protected marine environments.

funFact: Despite being a sea snail, the wavy lamellaria is so rarely encountered that it has only been officially observed once in all of New England - making it one of our region's most elusive marine creatures!
confusionNotes: Could potentially be confused with other small marine gastropods in tide pools, but the distinctive wavy patterns on the body when extended should help distinguish it. The key is waiting to see the animal emerge from its shell to observe the characteristic undulating features.
contextualKnowledge: The family name Velutinidae comes from 'velvet,' referring to the typically smooth, soft texture of these snails' bodies, though this doesn't mean they're actually velvety to the touch.
compareHints: Since there are no other Limneria species in our dataset for New England, compare the wavy lamellaria to other small marine snails in the velutinidae family by looking for its signature wavy body patterns. Other velutinids may have smooth bodies, but they lack the distinctive undulating ridges that give this species its common name.
